newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm on spillover from Chicago.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm on spillover from Chicago.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended steady to higher on spillover from a late buying spree in CBOT wheat and on unwinding of intermarket spreads with Chicago, traders said.
CBOT wheat gained late on buying by Refco and Continental Grain. Traders said KCBT wheat gained as players took profits in their CBOT/KCBT July spreads.

"We were following Chicago," a KCBT trader said. "But also Prudential, E. D. & F. Man, Wolcott Lincoln and Term Commodities all looked to be buying KC July and selling Chicago July at under 8-1/2 cents (per bushel)."
The intermarket July spread narrowed to close at 6-1/2 cents, after having traded last week around 15 cents.
Wheat weakened early as CBOT soybeans dropped on bearish input from the USDA crop report. But soybeans firmed and even turned mixed at one point in the midsession, traders said.
Additional pressure in KCBT wheat came from Monday's weekly state crop reports, which showed an improvement in HRW wheat condition.
KCBT wheat settled steady to 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with May unchanged at $4.12-1/4. March gained 1/4 cent to close at $4.39 and July settled up 1-1/4 cent at $3.78-1/2.
